elements.texte:
[cheerful] The marketing team wants to hold wellness workshops in town.

A workshop only takes place if the city has at least 2 customers.

So it needs these cities, with their number of customers.

Everything starts from the customers table, which holds one row per customer.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Having goes after group by and keeps the groups that meet the condition.

Here, only the cities with at least 2 customers are kept.

Each group takes the count star greater than or equal to 2 test: true or false?

Paris (4) and Lyon (2) pass the test: their groups are kept.

The 4 other cities have only one customer: their groups are left out.

Result: 2 rows, one for Lyon and one for Paris.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] And what if the workshop were only for customers aged 30 or over?

This condition is about each customer: it goes in the where.

Where sorts out the rows before the groups: 3 customers are left out.

Among them is Lucas Bernard, 28: in Lyon, there’s only one customer left.

Having then leaves out the Lyon group: only Paris remains.

Where sorts out the rows first, then having sorts out the groups.
